response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Cached login IDP set is keyed on the realm and fetch mode, but the delegate result varies with organizationId

Affected:
- model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:213-255

Explanation:
After a cache hit, the code resolves IDs through `session.identityProviders().getById(id)`. This returns the cached IDP models rather than the delegate's results. `getForLogin` in the delegate may wrap IDPs (the change to `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` says "idp might have been wrapped"). Wrapping is applied on the miss path through `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`, but not on the cache-hit path. The cache-hit path returns the raw cached model, so results differ depending on whether the cache is warm.

The first-load branch (`query == null`) also ignores the wrapping and re-reads through `getById`. This is inconsistent. In addition, the invalidated path returns different objects from the cached path. Apply the same wrapping to every returned model.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
identityProviders.add(createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(idp));
// or return identityProviders.stream().map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Login predicate change affects all callers and may disagree with the delegate's query

Affected:
- server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254

Explanation:
`getLoginPredicate()` now also requires that an IDP either has no organization or is marked broker-public. This predicate is shared by every caller. It is also used to decide whether to invalidate the caches. If the JPA `getForLogin` query implements its own filtering, then the cache invalidation decision and the actual query result can diverge. For example, an IDP linked to an org with `BROKER_PUBLIC` removed would be treated as non-login on update. Verify that the JPA query and the predicate are consistent for each `FetchMode`.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
// Ensure the JPA getForLogin applies the same org/public rules, or add tests covering
// toggling BROKER_PUBLIC on org-linked IDPs and invalidation.
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Removing or updating an org-linked IDP can leave stale ORG_ONLY and ALL entries

Affected:
- model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:403-418

Explanation:
On update, `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` skips invalidation when the login status and the organization ID are unchanged. But if the IDP's login-relevant state is stored on `original`, `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` is evaluated on a model from `getById` that may be a cached model. Also, `remove` calls `idpDelegate.getByAlias` unconditionally, which adds a DB lookup on every removal even when the cached entry exists. Finally, `remove` can pass a null `storedIdp` to `registerIDPInvalidation` when the IDP does not exist. This was previously the case only in the `isInvalid` branch.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);
if (storedIdp == null) return idpDelegate.remove(alias);
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Test
Title: Test cleanup registers removal of a non-existent alias

Affected:
- testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java:381
- testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java:425

Explanation:
The cleanup uses `identityProviders().get("alias")` (a literal) instead of the real alias. The created IDPs are never cleaned up, which can leak state into other tests, and the cleanup itself fails at teardown.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
String alias = "idp-alias-" + i;
getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias)::remove);
~~~
